title: Japan, Dec 2026 · 8 friends
who: A group of 8, all around 20 years old, all Asian; eight degenerates who love to drink, want to maximise every moment and love to do it all: Round1, streetwear and vintage, karaoke, izakaya nights, and one-of-a-kind group moments (Santa suits, wrestling, a dinner cruise). Plan C (data/japan-plan-c.md) is the real them.

wishes.text: Osaka base, but during the day we will commute to Kyoto/Nara as needed
Ending the night/nightlife in Osaka
If there are cool nightlife things to do in the neighbouring cities as well, include them
We love to drink
We want to maximise all the time we've got in the country
Round1
Shopping
We love to do it all
No go-karts
Look for money we can save by booking early or buying passes
Stays already booked: Ninja House in Toshima (Tokyo), Hot Spring Hakone Villa in Sengokuhara, Kujō House in Nishi-ku (Osaka), Garfield House in Shinjuku (Tokyo)
Christmas Day in Santa suits, the whole group, ending in a Round1 all-nighter in Osaka
The Grand Santa Parade in Umekita, Osaka (about 500 Santas, suits provided and yours to keep; needs a sign-up; Plan C had it on Tue 22 Dec)
Pro wrestling: Pro Wrestling NOAH Thanksgiving 2026 at Korakuen Hall (Plan C had Fri 18 Dec)
A B.LEAGUE basketball game: Tokyo Sunrockers at Toyota Arena Tokyo (Plan C had Sun 27 Dec)
A yakatabune dinner cruise with unlimited drinks on Sat 26 Dec, the night of the Odaiba fireworks
Hiroshima and Miyajima (floating torii, grilled oysters, okonomiyaki) if a day can be spared; otherwise Kyoto and Nara carry the Kansai days
Yunessun wine, sake and coffee baths in Hakone, and a villa wagyu cook-off on the Hakone night
A KFC Christmas party barrel on Christmas Eve
Fugu in Osaka
Morning sumo practice at a stable (Plan C: Arashio-beya in Ryōgoku) and a private omakase counter
A 24-hour onsen night (Thermae-yu in Kabukichō or Spa World in Shinsekai)
Streetwear, sneakers and vintage (Harajuku, Koenji, Shimokitazawa, Ameyoko, Amerikamura), Don Quijote and tax-free hauls
Karaoke (Manekineko, Big Echo, Karaokekan), arcades, izakaya and yokocho nights, standing bars, and the last-train problem solved properly
No nightclubs (a group rule from Plan C; ignore touts and bar invites in Kabukichō)
Legendary, not generic: nothing only there because it is on page one of every Tokyo or Kyoto itinerary, and no sit-down sightseeing filler between the big moments
Be bold: prefer one-of-a-kind, local-run, hard-to-book and group-scale things, and name a safe fallback beside every hard-to-book thing
At most two deliberate nights under 4 hours' sleep; any early start after a late night needs a reason (rope-drop at USJ, first light at Fushimi Inari)
Everyone stays together; every booking is for 8 at the same table or private room (8名で、同じテーブル/個室)
Plan C is the spine: keep what survives checking and replace what does not with something equally special

pace: Packed — maximise every day, including late nights out drinking, but at most two deliberate nights under 4 hours' sleep
